questions.q: What is a privilege in the Oracle Fusion security model?
options: A named user account with elevated rights
A report that lists every role in the system
The smallest grantable unit of permission to perform one specific action
A synonym for a job role
questions.explain: A privilege is the smallest unit of 'permission to do one thing,' such as voiding a payment. Privileges are granted to roles, not directly to users.

questions.q: A data security policy pairs which two things?
options: A username and a password
A job role and an abstract role
A privilege and a duty role
A condition (a filter on the data) and a set of allowed actions on a resource, attached to a role
questions.explain: A data security policy defines a condition (such as a business unit filter) plus allowable actions against a database resource, and is attached to a role.

questions.q: Which of the following is a classic example of an abstract role?
options: Accounts Payable Manager
General Ledger Accountant
Employee
US Business Unit Payables Data Role
questions.explain: Employee is the most common abstract role — it's granted regardless of specific job title and covers access every worker needs.

questions.q: How does a user account most commonly come to exist in Oracle Fusion Cloud?
options: It is purchased separately from the application
It is automatically created when a worker record is created
Every user account must be typed in manually by Oracle support
It is generated the first time someone tries to sign in
questions.explain: In most implementations, user account auto-creation triggers the moment a worker record (such as a new hire) is created.

questions.q: What does the Security Console's Simulate Navigator feature actually verify?
options: Which data rows a user can see once a page opens
Function security — which menu and task entries a role or user can reach
The user's password strength
Whether a journal entry balances
questions.explain: Simulate Navigator previews the Navigator menu structure available to a role or user, which confirms function security, not data security.

questions.q: What does a data access set primarily secure?
options: Which pages a user can open
Access to one or more ledgers or ledger sets, down to balancing segment values
Which privileges exist in the system
Password complexity rules
questions.explain: A data access set is General Ledger's mechanism for scoping access to ledgers or ledger sets, optionally down to specific balancing segment values.

questions.q: What does a 'security context' name in Oracle Fusion's security model?
options: The specific privilege a role grants
The specific enterprise-structure dimension that a data security grant is scoped by
The password policy applied to a user
The name of the job role itself
questions.explain: A security context identifies which dimension (such as Business Unit or Data Access Set) a particular data security grant applies to.

questions.q: Which task is used to assign a user access to a specific business unit alongside a job role?
options: Define Chart of Accounts
Manage Data Access for Users
Manage Bank Statements
Create Journal Approval Rules
questions.explain: Manage Data Access for Users, with the security context set to Business Unit, is used to grant a user access to a specific business unit.

questions.q: What is the general pattern that repeats across GL, AP, and AR security?
options: Every action is available to every job role equally
Only managers can ever use any of the three modules
Routine entry work sits in specialist-level duty roles, higher-risk/irreversible actions sit in manager-level duty roles, and data security scopes all of it
Data security only applies to General Ledger, never to AP or AR
questions.explain: All three modules separate routine, specialist-level entry work from higher-risk, manager-level actions (posting, approval, write-off), with data security scoping access throughout.

questions.q: At Castellan Robotics, where did the implementation team focus most of its actual configuration effort for the Payables job roles?
options: Deciding which business units each person's role assignment would cover, using the seeded roles mostly as delivered
Rebuilding the Accounts Payable Specialist role's duty roles from scratch
Removing all data security policies from every role
Renaming every seeded job role to match internal job titles
questions.explain: Most implementations use Oracle's seeded job roles largely as-is and focus configuration effort on data access (such as business unit assignment) rather than redesigning function access.

questions.q: Does Oracle Fusion automatically prevent a role from combining two conflicting duties, such as creating a supplier and approving its payments?
options: Yes, Oracle Fusion blocks any such role from ever being created
Only for General Ledger roles, never for Payables
Only if Advanced Access Controls is turned off
No — Oracle will provision a role combining both capabilities if an administrator builds and assigns it that way; SoD is a design discipline, not a built-in restriction
questions.explain: Oracle Fusion does not predefine or automatically enforce SoD business logic. Preventing conflicts is a role-design discipline applied by the implementation team.

questions.q: Why is reviewing the access audit report only once, right before go-live, considered insufficient?
options: Because it does not catch later drift, such as a role mapping over-provisioning access after a reorganization or a transferred employee keeping old access
Because the report can only be run one time ever
Because the report is only valid for 24 hours after go-live
Because Oracle requires it to be run only during implementation
questions.explain: Access drift happens over time as roles, mappings, and job assignments change, so recurring review (often quarterly) is needed to catch issues a one-time go-live check would miss.

questions.q: In Scenario 3, why did the regional controller's GL numbers look wrong even though her data access set was confirmed correct?
options: Because a balancing segment value had never been assigned a default ledger set during enterprise structure setup — a configuration gap, not a security problem
Because the problem was actually a security issue after all
Because her role was accidentally deleted
Because General Ledger does not support balancing segments
questions.explain: This scenario illustrates the Lesson 17 warning that not every 'wrong data' complaint is a security issue — this one was an enterprise structure setup gap.

questions.q: How is a higher-risk role that is NOT marked self-requestable typically requested?
options: It can never be requested or granted under any circumstances
Automatically, the same way as any self-requestable role
Only by the user editing their own account directly
Through a formal request (ticket, form, or similar) reviewed against actual job need and provisioned manually once approved
questions.explain: Roles not marked self-requestable require a formal, manual request process outside of self-service, reviewed and provisioned by an administrator.

questions.q: During which implementation phase does this lesson say segregation-of-duties review is cheapest to perform?
options: After go-live, once real tickets start arriving
SoD review timing makes no difference to cost
During role design, before people are provisioned the wrong combination of roles
Only during the external audit
questions.explain: Reviewing for SoD conflicts during role design is far cheaper than discovering and correcting conflicts after fifty people have already been provisioned.

questions.q: In the function security troubleshooting path, what should be checked after confirming the expected role was provisioned?
options: The user's data access set value
Whether the underlying data exists at all
The company's chart of accounts
Whether Simulate Navigator confirms the role includes the menu item or button in question
questions.explain: Simulate Navigator is the next step for confirming whether the provisioned role actually includes the function being tested.
